level.title: Master: Translation, Oratory and Teaching Hindi
goals: Translate between Hindi and English with register, idiom and rhythm intact.
Compress for subtitles and expand for voice-over without losing tone.
Deliver a structured speech, host a stage and handle a hostile question.
Read dohā and caupāī metre and the Braj/Awadhi grammar they carry.
Explain Hindi grammar to a learner, diagnose errors and design a lesson.

lessons.title: Idiom for Idiom, Not Word for Word
lessons.learn: A master translator asks what a phrase does, not what it says. ‘Break a leg’ is not टाँग तोड़ो; it is ‘जाओ, कमाल कर दो’. ‘दाल में कुछ काला है’ is not ‘something black in the lentils’ but ‘something fishy’. When no idiom matches, translate the function in plain words and keep the tone; when the image itself matters, keep it and gloss lightly.

grammar.title: The three-way choice for every idiom
grammar.explain: (1) समतुल्य मुहावरा — a target idiom with the same function and register: ‘the last straw’ → ‘ऊँट की पीठ पर आख़िरी तिनका’ (same image, happily) ; ‘once in a blue moon’ → ‘कभी-कभार / ईद का चाँद’. (2) सपाट भावानुवाद — plain sense when no idiom fits: ‘he's on the fence’ → ‘वह अभी तय नहीं कर पाया’. (3) बिम्ब रखकर टिप्पणी — keep the image when it carries culture: ‘उसने नमक-हलाली निभाई’ → ‘he kept faith with the salt he had eaten — stayed loyal’. Never choose (3) in dialogue subtitles; never choose (1) if the target idiom shifts register (a rustic proverb inside a courtroom speech).
grammar.pattern: function + register → equivalent idiom / plain sense / image + gloss

lessons.title: Register and Rhythm Across Languages
lessons.learn: English formality lives in Latin-root vocabulary and passive voice; Hindi formality lives in tatsam vocabulary, आप-forms and compound verbs like किया जाना. A legal clause, a tender love note and a street argument each need their own Hindi lexical layer. Beyond words, sentence length and stress must be re-tuned: Hindi carries emphasis by word order and particles (ही, तो, भी), English by stress and cleft sentences.

grammar.title: Carrying emphasis without italics
grammar.explain: English: ‘It was RAM who broke it’ / ‘It was Ram who broke it’. Hindi has no stress marking in print; it uses (a) particles — ‘राम ने ही तोड़ा’ (only/precisely Ram), ‘राम ने तो तोड़ा’ (as for Ram…), ‘राम ने भी तोड़ा’ (Ram too); (b) fronting — moving the emphasised word to the start or just before the verb; (c) cleft-like ‘तोड़ने वाला राम था’. Register: formal Hindi prefers tatsam nouns + light verb (निर्णय लिया गया), informal prefers Persian/tadbhav + simple verb (फ़ैसला कर लिया). Match sentence length to genre: legal Hindi tolerates long sentences; dialogue does not.
grammar.pattern: English stress/cleft → Hindi ही/तो/भी + fronting ; Latin-root formality → tatsam + किया जाना

lessons.title: Subtitling and Voice-over: Compress, Expand, Sync
lessons.learn: A subtitle gets about 35 Devanagari characters per line, two lines, on screen for under six seconds; the translator must cut without losing the joke or the threat. A voice-over has the opposite problem: Hindi often runs longer than English, so the dub script must be timed to lip-flaps and breath. Masters cut function words and hedges first, names and numbers never.

grammar.title: What to cut, what to keep
grammar.explain: Cut order for subtitles: (1) fillers and hedges (देखिए, दरअसल, मेरा मतलब); (2) vocatives after the first (भाई, यार); (3) redundant auxiliaries where tense is clear (‘जा रहा हूँ’ → ‘जा रहा’) ; (4) one of two synonyms. Keep: proper names, numbers, negation, the punch-word of a joke, any threat or promise. For dubbing, expand or contract with light verbs (कर देना / कर लेना) and vocatives to hit syllable count; place the stressed Hindi word on the visible lip-closure (प/ब/म) where possible.
grammar.pattern: subtitle: ≤2 lines × ~35 chars, cut fillers → keep names/numbers/negation ; dub: match syllables + stressed labials to lip-flaps

units.title: Public Hindi: Stage, Speech and Debate

lessons.title: Anchoring a Stage: Mañc Sañcālan
lessons.learn: Indian stage anchoring has a liturgy: welcome, lamp-lighting, introduction of dignitaries in rank order, a couplet before each item, thanks at the end. The anchor's Hindi is slightly elevated, rhythmic, and never upstages the performer. Masters prepare transitions in advance and improvise only the filler when a performer is late.

grammar.title: Formulae and the rank-order rule
grammar.explain: Opening: ‘मंच पर विराजमान … , आदरणीय … , एवं उपस्थित सभी सुधीजनों को सादर नमस्कार।’ Rank order: chief guest → presiding officer → guests of honour → host institution head; mention names with designation first time, designation only after. Invitation formula: ‘मैं … जी से सादर अनुरोध करूँगा/करूँगी कि वे मंच पर पधारें।’ Item transition: one line of verse or a one-sentence bridge, then ‘प्रस्तुत है …’. Applause cue: ‘करतल ध्वनि से स्वागत कीजिए’. Closing: धन्यवाद ज्ञापन by someone else, anchor only announces it. Keep each anchor turn under 40 seconds.
grammar.pattern: नमस्कार (rank order) → दीप प्रज्वलन → स्वागत → items with bridge + ‘प्रस्तुत है’ → धन्यवाद ज्ञापन

lessons.title: The Structured Speech: Hook, Three Points, Return
lessons.learn: A persuasive Hindi speech opens with a hook — a story, a question or a line of verse — states its one idea, develops three points with a concrete example each, and returns to the opening image in the last sentence. Rhetoric lives in तीन की लय (triads), अनुप्रास, deliberate repetition (पुनरावृत्ति) and the pause. Masters write for the ear: short clauses, spoken connectors, no sentence they cannot say in one breath.

grammar.title: Writing for the ear
grammar.explain: Spoken syntax: subject + short predicate; put the key word last in the clause where Hindi naturally stresses it. Triads: ‘न सड़क थी, न स्कूल था, न उम्मीद थी।’ Anaphora: begin three consecutive sentences with the same phrase (‘हम वे लोग हैं जो…’). Rhetorical question followed by the answer. Contrast pair: ‘सवाल पैसे का नहीं, नीयत का है।’ Mark pauses in the script with ‘/’; a pause before the key word doubles its weight. Conclusion: do not summarise; return to the opening image, changed.
grammar.pattern: hook → one idea → 3 points (each: claim + concrete example + line to remember) → return to the hook

lessons.title: Debate and the Hostile Question
lessons.learn: In a Hindi debate or press Q&A the master does four things in order: acknowledge (‘अच्छा सवाल है’ only if it is), reframe the loaded premise, answer in one sentence, then bridge to the point they want to make. The tone stays warm; the grammar stays declarative. Never repeat a hostile phrase — repeat the correction instead.

grammar.title: ABAB: acknowledge, reframe, answer, bridge
grammar.explain: Acknowledge: ‘आपने ज़रूरी मुद्दा उठाया।’ Reframe the loaded premise without repeating it: Q ‘आपकी नाकाम योजना पर कितना पैसा बर्बाद हुआ?’ → ‘योजना का पहला चरण पूरा हुआ है; व्यय और परिणाम दोनों सार्वजनिक हैं।’ Answer in one declarative sentence with a number if you have one. Bridge: ‘और असल बात यह है कि …’ / ‘इससे भी ज़रूरी सवाल यह है कि …’. Rebuttal in debate: name the opponent's claim neutrally (‘विपक्ष का कहना है कि …’), give the missing fact, conclude with ‘इसलिए’. Composure devices: slow down, lower volume, use आप throughout.
grammar.pattern: स्वीकार → पुनर्संरचना (don't echo the slur) → एक-वाक्य उत्तर (+ number) → सेतु

examples.t: प्रश्न: ‘आपकी नाकाम योजना पर कितना पैसा बर्बाद हुआ?’ उत्तर: ‘योजना का पहला चरण पूरा हुआ है — बारह करोड़ व्यय, चार सौ घर। असल सवाल यह है कि दूसरे चरण में गति कैसे बढ़े।’

examples.en: Q: ‘How much money was wasted on your failed scheme?’ A: ‘The first phase is complete — twelve crore spent, four hundred homes. The real question is how to speed up phase two.’

examples.t: विपक्ष का कहना है कि निजी वाहनों पर रोक से व्यापार प्रभावित होगा। आँकड़ा यह है कि पैदल-क्षेत्रों में दुकानों की बिक्री बढ़ी है। इसलिए रोक व्यापार के विरुद्ध नहीं, उसके पक्ष में है।
examples.r: vipakṣ kā kahnā hai ki nijī vāhanõ par rok se vyāpār prabhāvit hogā. ā̃kṛā yah hai ki paidal-kṣetrõ mẽ dukānõ kī bikrī baṛhī hai. islie rok vyāpār ke viruddh nahī̃, uske pakṣ mẽ hai.

examples.en: ‘I understand your point, and I disagree — because …’ (composure formula)

lessons.title: Dohā and Caupāī: Metre and Old Grammar
lessons.learn: The two workhorse metres of pre-modern Hindi: दोहा (two lines of 13+11 mātrās each, ending the second half on a short syllable) and चौपाई (four quarters of 16 mātrās). They carry Braj and Awadhi grammar: है → अहै/है, का/की → को/केरि, ने absent, -हि/-हिं object marker, verb forms like करत (does), कीन्ह (did), होइ (be). A master counts mātrās and reads the old forms without a gloss.

vocab.en: Awadhi (literary dialect of the Rāmcaritmānas tradition)

grammar.title: Counting mātrās and decoding old verb forms
grammar.explain: Mātrā count: अ इ उ and consonant+short vowel = 1; आ ई ऊ ए ऐ ओ औ, anusvāra-bearing syllables and syllables before a conjunct = 2. दोहा: each line = 13 mātrās, यति, 11 mātrās; the 11 ends in गुरु-लघु (e.g. ‘होय’, ‘जाय’). चौपाई: 16 + 16 per line, two lines. Old forms: करत/करति = करता/करती; कीन्ह/कियो = किया; अहै/है = है; होइ/होय = हो; -हि/-हिं = को (object/dative); केर/केरि/कर = का/की; मोहि/तोहि = मुझे/तुझे; जेहि/तेहि = जिसे/उसे; Braj -औ ending on adjectives (बड़ौ, छोटौ); no ने with past tense.
grammar.pattern: दोहा 13 | 11 × 2 (end गुरु-लघु) ; चौपाई 16 | 16 × 2 ; old forms → modern equivalents

examples.t: (EkGuru teaching dohā) साँझ ढले दीया जले, घर-घर बाँटे प्रीत। / जो अपनों को छाँव दे, वही जगत की रीत॥ — 13|11, 13|11; ends ‘प्रीत’, ‘रीत’ (गुरु-लघु)
examples.r: sā̃jh ḍhale dīyā jale, ghar-ghar bā̃ṭe prīt. / jo apnõ ko chā̃v de, vahī jagat kī rīt.
examples.en: At dusk the lamp is lit, sharing love house to house; / he who shades his own — that is the way of the world.

examples.t: (EkGuru teaching caupāī, Awadhi grammar) भोर भए पंछी सब बोलहिं। / खेत किसान मगन मन डोलहिं॥
examples.r: bhor bhae pañchī sab bolahĩ. / khet kisān magan man ḍolahĩ.
examples.en: Dawn having come, all the birds call; / in the field the farmer sways, glad at heart.  (बोलहिं = बोलते हैं, भए = हुए)

examples.t: मोहि तोहि केरि बात सुनावहु = मुझे तेरी बात सुनाओ
examples.r: mohi tohi keri bāt sunāvahu = mujhe terī bāt sunāo
examples.en: tell me your tale (मोहि = मुझे, तोहि केरि = तेरी, -हु imperative)

mistakes: Counting every syllable as 1: a long vowel or a syllable before a conjunct is 2.
Reading ‘करत’ as a past tense: it is present/habitual (करता).

dialogue.t: ‘बोलहिं’ का क्या मतलब है? कोई पुराना शब्द है?
dialogue.r: ‘bolahĩ’ kā kyā matlab hai? koī purānā śabd hai?
dialogue.en: What does ‘bolahĩ’ mean? Some old word?

dialogue.t: शब्द वही है — बोलना। ‘-हिं’ अवधी का बहुवचन वर्तमान है: बोलते हैं।
dialogue.r: śabd vahī hai — bolnā. ‘-hĩ’ avadhī kā bahuvacan vartmān hai: bolte haĩ.
dialogue.en: Same word — to speak. ‘-hĩ’ is the Awadhi plural present: they speak.

dialogue.t: और मात्राएँ कैसे गिनूँ?
dialogue.r: aur mātrāẽ kaise ginū̃?
dialogue.en: And how do I count mātrās?

dialogue.t: भो-र-भ-ए: 2+1+1+1 = 5 … पूरी पंक्ति सोलह। गिनकर देखो, चौपाई ख़ुद बताएगी।
dialogue.r: bho-ra-bha-e: 2+1+1+1 = 5 … pūrī paṅkti solah. ginkar dekho, caupāī khud batāegī.
dialogue.en: bho-ra-bha-e: 2+1+1+1 = 5 … the whole line sixteen. Count it; the caupāī tells you itself.

lessons.title: Explaining Hindi to a Learner
lessons.learn: Knowing Hindi and explaining Hindi are different skills. A master teacher gives the rule in one sentence, then a minimal pair, then a trap and its fix — and never says ‘it just sounds right’. The three explanations every teacher must own: ergative ने, grammatical gender, and the compound-verb (जाना/लेना/देना) system.

grammar.title: Three one-sentence rules with minimal pairs
grammar.explain: ERGATIVE: ‘In the perfective past, a transitive verb's subject takes ने and the verb agrees with the object.’ Pair: लड़का सोया (intransitive, agrees with boy) vs लड़के ने रोटी खाई (agrees with रोटी, f.). Trap: लाना, भूलना, बोलना take no ने. GENDER: ‘-आ nouns are usually masculine, -ई usually feminine; everything else, learn with the noun and check the adjective.’ Pair: बड़ा कमरा / बड़ी मेज़. Trap: पानी (m.), दही (m.), किताब (f.). COMPOUND VERBS: ‘The second verb adds attitude, not meaning: लेना = for self, देना = for others, जाना = completeness/change, डालना = abruptness.’ Pair: उसने खाना खाया / खा लिया (finished, for himself). Trap: no compound verb with negation in neutral speech (नहीं खाया, not नहीं खा लिया).
grammar.pattern: rule (1 sentence) → minimal pair → trap + fix

examples.t: लड़का सोया। / लड़के ने रोटी खाई।
examples.r: laṛkā soyā. / laṛke ne roṭī khāī.
examples.en: The boy slept. / The boy ate the roti. (verb agrees with roti, feminine)

examples.t: बड़ा कमरा, बड़ी मेज़ — पर ठंडा पानी, ताज़ा दही।
examples.r: baṛā kamrā, baṛī mez — par ṭhaṇḍā pānī, tāzā dahī.
examples.en: big room (m.), big table (f.) — but cold water (m.), fresh curd (m.)

examples.t: उसने चाय पी। / उसने चाय पी ली। / उसने चाय पी डाली।
examples.r: usne cāy pī. / usne cāy pī lī. / usne cāy pī ḍālī.
examples.en: She drank the tea. / She finished her tea. / She gulped the tea down.

mistakes: Explaining ने as ‘past tense marker’: it marks transitive perfective agents, and the verb then agrees with the object.
Telling a learner compound verbs are ‘optional flavour’: in a finished action ‘खा लिया’ is the unmarked form and plain ‘खाया’ can sound abrupt.

dialogue.t: ‘मैंने स्कूल गया’ — यह ग़लत क्यों है? पास्ट टेंस तो है।
dialogue.r: ‘maĩne skūl gayā’ — yah galat kyõ hai? pāsṭ ṭens to hai.
dialogue.en: ‘maĩne school gayā’ — why is this wrong? It's past tense.

dialogue.t: ने का नियम पास्ट का नहीं, सकर्मक का है। ‘जाना’ का कोई कर्म नहीं — इसलिए ‘मैं स्कूल गया’।
dialogue.r: ne kā niyam pāsṭ kā nahī̃, sakarmak kā hai. ‘jānā’ kā koī karm nahī̃ — islie ‘maĩ skūl gayā’.
dialogue.en: The ने rule is about transitivity, not past. ‘To go’ has no object — so ‘maĩ school gayā’.

dialogue.t: तो ‘मैंने किताब पढ़ी’ में ‘पढ़ी’ किताब की वजह से?
dialogue.r: to ‘maĩne kitāb paṛhī’ mẽ ‘paṛhī’ kitāb kī vajah se?
dialogue.en: So in ‘maĩne kitāb paṛhī’, ‘paṛhī’ is because of kitāb?

dialogue.t: बिल्कुल — क्रिया कर्म से सहमत होती है। अब न्यूनतम युग्म बनाओ: ‘पत्र’ के साथ।
dialogue.r: bilkul — kriyā karm se sahmat hotī hai. ab nyūntam yugm banāo: ‘patra’ ke sāth.
dialogue.en: Exactly — the verb agrees with the object. Now make a minimal pair with ‘patra’.

practice.q: Write a one-sentence rule + minimal pair for a learner who wrote ‘उसने आया’.
practice.answer: Rule: ने only with transitive verbs in the perfective; आना is intransitive. Pair: वह आया / उसने चिट्ठी भेजी।

practice.q: Diagnose and fix: ‘मेरी पानी ठंडी है।’
practice.answer: पानी is masculine despite ending in -ई: मेरा पानी ठंडा है। Trap list: पानी, दही, घी, मोती (m.).

practice.q: Explain the difference in one sentence each: ‘उसने दरवाज़ा खोला’ / ‘उसने दरवाज़ा खोल दिया’.
practice.answer: खोला = plain fact; खोल दिया = completed and done for someone else / outward (देना adds ‘for the other’ and completion).

practice.q: Which verb takes no ने in the past even though it looks transitive?
practice.answer: लाना

practice.q: In ‘राम ने दो चिट्ठियाँ लिखीं’, the verb agrees with ____.
practice.answer: चिट्ठियाँ (the object)

practice.q: Rewrite this teacher explanation so it gives a rule, not ‘it sounds right’: ‘बस ऐसा ही बोलते हैं — “खा लिया” ज़्यादा अच्छा लगता है।’
practice.answer: ‘लेना’ क्रिया पूर्णता और ‘अपने लिए’ का भाव जोड़ती है; समाप्त हुए काम के लिए ‘खा लिया’ सामान्य रूप है, जबकि अकेला ‘खाया’ रूखा या अधूरा लग सकता है। युग्म: खाना खाया? / खाना खा लिया?

practice.q: Write a 10-minute micro-lesson plan in Hindi for teaching ने to A2 learners: objective, warm-up, rule, 3 minimal pairs, 5-item drill, exit question.
practice.answer: (Model) उद्देश्य: शिक्षार्थी सकर्मक/अकर्मक भेद से ने का प्रयोग कर सकें। वार्म-अप: ‘कल तुमने क्या किया?’ उत्तरों को दो स्तंभों में बाँटें। नियम: एक वाक्य। युग्म: वह सोया/उसने खाना खाया; वह हँसी/उसने कहानी सुनाई; वे आए/उन्होंने फ़ोन किया। ड्रिल: पाँच वाक्य, ने लगाओ या मत लगाओ। निकास-प्रश्न: ‘मैंने स्कूल गया’ क्यों ग़लत है?

practice.answer: object

practice.answer: बड़ा कमरा, बड़ी मेज़ — पर ठंडा पानी, ताज़ा दही।

practice.answer: शिक्षार्थी

lessons.title: Feedback, Error Analysis and the Learner's Path
lessons.learn: The last mastery is reading another person's Hindi and knowing what to say. Masters sort errors into slips (learner knows the rule), developmental errors (rule not yet acquired) and transfer errors (from English or the mother tongue), correct only what the learner can fix at their level, and phrase feedback as a recast or a question before a correction.

grammar.title: Three error types, three responses
grammar.explain: SLIP (learner self-corrects if asked): respond with a raised eyebrow or ‘फिर से?’. DEVELOPMENTAL (e.g. A2 learner omitting ने): recast — repeat their sentence correctly in your reply, no comment — and plan a lesson. TRANSFER (English word order ‘मैं जाता हूँ स्कूल’; Marathi speaker's ‘मला’ patterns): name the source gently: ‘अंग्रेज़ी में क्रिया बीच में आती है, हिंदी में अंत में।’ Priority: errors that block meaning > frequent errors > level-appropriate errors; ignore the rest for now. Written feedback formula: one thing done well (specific) → one pattern to fix (with rule + pair) → one task.
grammar.pattern: classify (चूक / विकासात्मक / अंतरण) → choose response (prompt / recast / explain) → prioritise by meaning, frequency, level

examples.t: शिक्षार्थी: ‘कल मैं देखा फ़िल्म।’ शिक्षक (recast): ‘अच्छा, कल आपने फ़िल्म देखी! कौन-सी?’

(b) दुकानदार का विवरण जीवंत है। एक पैटर्न: भूतकाल में सकर्मक क्रिया के साथ ने और क्रिया वाक्य के अंत में — मैं बाज़ार गया / मैंने एक किताब ख़रीदी। (c) इन्हीं चार वाक्यों को ने और क्रिया-अंत नियम से दोबारा लिखें।

culture.text: Mastery in Hindi has always meant moving between worlds. The court poets of Braj and Awadh wrote in metres whose mātrās a village singer can still count; the dubbing studios of Mumbai turn Hollywood into Hindi against a stopwatch; the school annual day keeps a liturgy of lamp, couplet and applause; and the language classroom, from Jaipur to New Jersey, asks the same three questions about ने, gender and compound verbs. A master translator, anchor, teacher or debater is not someone who knows more words, but someone who knows which world a sentence belongs to and can carry it, intact, into another.

reading.text: रेडियो स्टूडियो में घड़ी रात के ग्यारह बजा रही थी और अनुवादक की मेज़ पर एक अंग्रेज़ी वृत्तचित्र की स्क्रिप्ट खुली थी। वाक्य था — ‘The river doesn't negotiate.’ चार शब्द, डेढ़ सेकंड का होंठ-मिलान, और उसके पीछे पूरी फ़िल्म का भाव। ‘नदी बातचीत नहीं करती’ — सही, पर सपाट। ‘नदी समझौता नहीं करती’ — बेहतर, पर एक सिलेबल ज़्यादा। उसने आँखें बंद कीं और दादी की आवाज़ याद की, जो हर बरसात में कहती थीं — ‘नदी किसी की नहीं सुनती।’ पाँच सिलेबल में छह नहीं समाते, पर ‘नदी सुनती नहीं’ — तीन शब्द, लय वही, और आख़िरी ‘नहीं’ पर होंठ बंद। उसने लिखा, मिटाया, फिर लिखा। निर्देशक ने हेडफ़ोन उतारकर कहा, ‘यही। यह अनुवाद नहीं है, यह वही बात है।’ अनुवादक मुस्कुराया। बीस साल में उसने यही सीखा था — शब्दकोश बताता है कि शब्द क्या कहते हैं; भाषा बताती है कि वे क्या करते हैं। और मास्टर वह है जो दूसरे को पहले सुनता है।

listening.script: नमस्कार। आज की कार्यशाला तीन सत्रों में है। पहले सत्र में हम एक अंग्रेज़ी दृश्य के उपशीर्षक बनाएँगे — दो पंक्तियाँ, पैंतीस अक्षर, नाम और संख्या कभी नहीं कटेंगे। दूसरे सत्र में मंच संचालन का अभ्यास — नामों का क्रम याद रखिए: मुख्य अतिथि, अध्यक्ष, विशिष्ट अतिथि, प्राचार्य। तीसरे सत्र में आप एक शिक्षार्थी का निबंध जाँचेंगे — तीस ग़लतियाँ नहीं, एक पैटर्न। और हाँ, अंत में एक दोहा — अपना लिखा हुआ, तेरह और ग्यारह मात्राओं में। कलम तैयार रखिए।

mistakes.why: Give a rule and a minimal pair, never ‘it just sounds right’.

task.title: Master's portfolio
task.instructions: Assemble a four-piece portfolio in Hindi. (1) Translate a two-minute English scene as subtitles (2×35 rule) and separately as a dub script timed to the lips; annotate three idiom decisions with strategy 1/2/3. (2) Write and record a three-minute speech on a civic issue in your city with a hook, three points and a return; mark pauses with ‘/’. (3) Compose two original dohās on any theme, with a mātrā ledger for each half-line, and modernise one classical-style caupāī (your own composition is fine). (4) Take a real learner text (or write a plausible A2 one), produce an error table (type / rule / priority), 80 words of feedback in the praise → pattern → task formula, and a ten-minute micro-lesson plan targeting the top pattern.
